verdict.reasoning: Patient reports headache 'been going on for a few days' and 'around three days ago, maybe.'
Patient states pain is 'all over my head, but like mainly, um, around my right eye,' consistent with global headache worse in right periorbital region.
Patient says headache 'is there all the time, but like sometimes it's stronger' and rates it 'probably a eight' on a 1–10 scale.
Patient describes it as 'kind of, it's dull but sometimes it gets a bit sharper' and that it 'developed gradually... the first day it just started when I was at work.'
Transcript confirms it has 'been going on for a few days' and is 'getting worse over the last three days,' but does not say it is specifically 'worse in the morning.'

Photophobia: 'now like light is quite annoying, my eyes... it hurts'; visual phenomena: 'this like weird shooting lights'; nausea: 'I'm like basically, I I'm sick with the headache'; difficulty focusing: 'it's hard to focus though.'

Vision loss/blurry: 'Not loss of vision, I wouldn't say'; doctor asks about 'blurry vision' and no affirmative response; speech difficulty: 'Any difficulty with speaking...?' Patient: 'No.' Limb weakness: 'Any... weakness in your arms and legs?' Patient: 'No.' Head injury: 'any recent head injuries at all?' Patient: 'Uh, no.' Fever and rash: 'Any temperatures, or fevers?' 'No.' 'Any rashes at all...?' 'Mm, no not that I've noticed.'
Patient: 'I mean I had [headaches]... usually after I I take uh Ibuprofen it kind of goes away. So, but this time it's just not.'

No regular meds: 'do you take any regular medication?' Patient: 'Uh, no no.' Ibuprofen use: 'I tried uh Ibuprofen... for the last two days' and later 'three a day.' Minimal relief: 'But it doesn't really help, no.'
Doctor: 'Do you have any allergies to any medications?' Patient: 'Mm not that I know of.'
Doctor: 'Are you otherwise fit and well... do you have any other medical history?' Patient: 'Yeah, I think so. It's just the headache.'
Patient: 'my sister's, like better... it's very rare. But my mom's is like quite bad... usually when there's like a season changing.'
Living situation: 'I live with housemates. So, three of them. So we're four.' Work: 'I work in IT. So I work with computers a lot.'
'Do you wear glasses?' Patient: 'Yes, I do.' Eye exam: 'Have you had any recent eye check...?' Patient: 'No.'
Doctor: 'Do you drink or smoke at all?' Patient: 'I socially smoke. And I drink only socially.'
Patient: 'it's been a bit stressful, kicking off a new project. But um, yeah nothing out of the ordinary, really.' This supports mild work stress.
Doctor: 'I do think this could be, a headache very similar to a migraine,' and symptoms include photophobia, 'weird shooting lights,' and feeling 'sick with the headache,' consistent with nausea.
Doctor: 'You can take up to two tablets, three times a day... Or, I can prescribe you something stronger, like Naproxen... We can also add in other, painkillers like, Paracetamol, or Codeine.'
Doctor: 'It may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out what's... if there's any triggers.'

Doctor: 'I'd like you to come back and see me, in about uh, a week's time, week to two weeks' time... If you are having more frequent episodes... we can think about giving you medications as, prophylactic.'

Doctor: 'if your headaches aren't getting any better, or they're getting worse... give me a call, or come back... if you're having any problems with your vision, or weakness in your arms and legs, or you're just not feeling very well.'

Earlier, doctor advises: 'if you feel that you are, your eyes are straining. Um I would always recommend having a repeat eye test done.' This supports arranging a repeat eye test if ongoing eye strain.
